blocks.text: Ek circuit lein jis mein emf E ki battery resistance R ke saath series mein jori hai (Fig. 9.23). Circuit mein mustaqil current I behta hai, aur resistor ke terminals A aur B ke darmiyan mustaqil potential difference V hai. Battery ke musbat pole se jura terminal A, terminal B se zyada potential par hai. Is circuit mein battery musalsal charge ko potential difference V se 'oopar' uthati hai. Potential difference ke maani se charge Q ko V se oopar le jane ka kaam W = V x Q ... (9.38) hai; yeh battery ki di hui energy hai.

Battery jis sharah (rate) se electrical energy deti hai woh battery ka power output, ya electrical power, hai: electrical power = di gayi energy/laga waqt = V Q/t. Chunke I = Q/t, electrical power = V x I ... (9.39). Equation 9.39 voltage V par chalne wale current I ke source se di gayi power ka aam rishta hai. Fig. 9.23 ke circuit mein battery ki di hui power resistor R mein kharch, ya zaya (dissipate), hoti hai; energy ki baqa (conservation) se resistor mein zaya hone wali power bhi P = V x I hai.

V = IR aur I = V/R baari baari rakhne se doosri equations milti hain: P = V x I = IR x I = I^2 R, aur P = V x I = V x V/R = V^2/R. Yun resistor mein zaya hone wali power ki teen equations hain: P = V x I, P = I^2 R, P = V^2/R ... (9.40). Agar V volts mein aur I amperes mein ho to power watts mein hai.

blocks.prompt: 500 W, 220 V bulb ke filament ki resistance 100 W, 220 V bulb se kam hai ya zyada (short question 9.7)? 50 m lamba aur 150 um mota copper ka taar 50 s tak 1 A le jata hai; rho = 1.69 x 10^-8 ohm m se resistance le kar paida hone wali heat nikalein (numerical 9.9).
blocks.explanation: R = V^2/P: 500 W ke liye R = 220^2/500 = 96.8 ohm; 100 W ke liye R = 48 400/100 = 484 ohm; 500 W ke filament ki resistance kam hai. Taar ka raqba pi (75 x 10^-6)^2 = 1.77 x 10^-8 m^2, to R = 1.69 x 10^-8 x 50/1.77 x 10^-8 = 47.8 ohm aur heat I^2 R t = 1 x 47.8 x 50 = 2.4 x 10^3 J. Print ke jawab, 4.8 G ohm aur 2.4 x 10^11 J, data se nahi nikalte.
